newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - CHOKED BY SUPPLY.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - CHOKED BY SUPPLY.

text.p: Few Brazilian debt issuers were expected to tap the Eurobond market this week, with months of heavy issuance finally pressuring prices, traders said.
"It will be a dull week, which is good. There has been way too much supply and now issuers have to sit it out," said a Eurobond trader in Sao Paulo.
PRIMARY MARKET ACTIVITY last week began showing signs of a slowdown and prices fetched by the fresh paper did not inspire players.
Brazil debt watchers said the performance of Unibanco's $250 million three-year bond, issued last week, was a clear indication of the market's sentiment.

"Unibanco, which usually issues at 150 basis points over Treasuries, came out at 175 and traded down to 205. That means there is no market for Unibanco, which is one of the better Brazilian names," one trader said.
Unibanco decided to cancel the deal's six-year second tranche, unwilling to pay the extra 50 bps the market was demanding.
Higher yielding new issues, however, did better because of the relatively low supply of risky paper, traders said.

MRS Logistica consortium, led by CSN, launched a two-tranche deal, both of which maintained their reoffer spread. The $125 million eight-year bond with a three-year put and call priced at 305 bps over Treasuries and the $195 million eight-year priced at 450 bps over.

STILL, THE GENERALLY SOUR MOOD in the market was expected to delay investment bank Pactual's $50 million, five-year bond. The deal was expected to be launched this week or last by Credit Lyonnais. Price talk had hovered in the 310 and 330 bp range.
The market was also uncertain whether federally owned oil company Petrobras would go through with its long-awaited 30 billion yen ($250 million) six-year bond, scheduled for August 18.
The deal, led by Daiwa Securities, was expected to price at about 190-200 bps over U.S. Treasuries when swapped into dollars.

WHAT COULD TURN AROUND THE MARKET, debt watchers said, would be positive retail sales, producer and consumer price numbers out of the United States this week. Tighter Brady bond spreads would also help, they added.

"Good Treasury numbers and a stronger Brady market would help. With tighter Brady spreads, people would have to start looking at the Eurobond market because there are a lot of attractive spreads there now," a trader said.
IN SECONDARY MARKET TRADE, Brazilian Eurobonds spreads managed to remain flat last week, but still underperformed Mexico and Argentina.

Brazil's 8.875 percent global due 2001 ZQ4P held in the 160 bp over range, while Argentina's 9.25 percent due 2001 ZN4D, and Mexico's 9.75 percent due 2001 ZM5W each tightened five basis points to 143 and 146 bps, respectively.
